title: Do not carry letters reserved to Australia Post
what: Do not collect, carry or deliver letters within Australia, which Australia Post has the exclusive right to carry, unless an exception applies (such as letters over 250 grams, or a charge of at least 4 times the standard postage rate).

sources.title: Australian Postal Corporation Act 1989
sources.quote: Subject to section 30, Australia Post has the exclusive right to carry letters within Australia, whether the letters originated within or outside Australia.

reach.note: Calibration: coded for the calibration classes; other postal and courier classes follow in phase C.

sources.title: Australian Postal Corporation Act 1989
sources.quote: Subject to section 30, Australia Post has the exclusive right to carry letters within Australia, whether the letters originated within or outside Australia.

sources.title: Australian Postal Corporation Act 1989
sources.quote: (a) the carriage of a letter weighing more than 250 grams unless the letter consists of an envelope, packet, parcel, container or wrapper containing 2 or more separate letters;

sources.title: Australian Postal Corporation Act 1989
sources.quote: (e) the carriage of a letter within Australia for a charge or fee that is at least 4 times the then rate of postage for the carriage within Australia of a standard postal article by ordinary post;

assessment.summary: A legal monopoly on carrying ordinary letters. It shuts out rivals in a market that is now small and shrinking, so its cost to productivity is limited.

marks.reason: Rivals are barred by law from carrying ordinary letters: an exclusive right.

assessment.confidence_note: Marks from the register's assessment of the same law (cth-australia-post-reserved-services). The restriction is explicit; letter volumes have fallen, so the market it closes is small.
